name: Web document — Wikipedia (horizontal)
description: A recognizable Wikipedia article on a transparent overlay, as a clean backdrop for the channel's hand-pulled highlight. Faithful site look BY DESIGN: Wikipedia Vector light skin (white #ffffff bg, dark #202122 ink, serif article title + section heading each with the signature thin underline rule, italic 'From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia' subtitle, sans body), inside a browser window whose address bar shows the URL — NO Syntax collage chrome (no torn edge / grit / hard offset shadow), and NO CSS glow on the captured card. Because the page is light, the highlight runs in the light (multiply) blend mode — dark body ink stays readable under the amber band, exactly as on paper. The emissive 'web page on a backlit display' look is a TypeGPU shaderPass (subpixel emission, backlight bloom, escaping-bezel halo, viewport-edge defocus), not Pack chrome. ~6s: card settles in, the highlighter draws on over the hero line (~1.2→2.4s), then a long static hold a creator can freeze/extend. Transparent WebM overlay, composited over footage.

content.title: Program optimization
content.body:
In computer science, program optimization is the process of modifying a software system to make some aspect of it work more efficiently or use fewer resources. A guiding principle is that optimization should follow measurement: [highlight]a performance bottleneck is usually a small section of code executed very frequently[/highlight], rather than the component a developer first suspects.

Profilers locate these sections by sampling or instrumenting a running program. Once a hot path is identified, a single change — removing redundant work from an inner loop, caching a result, or avoiding I/O on each iteration — can yield disproportionate gains, while effort spent elsewhere has negligible effect.
